findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

This PR rewrites `SKILL.md` from an older four-capability snapshot and lands `version: "1.6.2"` plus a four-capability frontmatter `description`, while `main` (base) already ships `version: "2.5.1"` and a five-capability router that includes `apply-review`. Merging as-is would publish a major documentation/contract regression to the skills.sh source-of-truth path.

**Fix:** rebase onto current `main` and re-apply only the narrative reframe (title, two-audiences framing, Surface column, section order, Default-flow header) on top of the live five-capability / v2 content. Do not carry forward `1.6.2` or the four-capability description.

**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

The capabilities table stops at four rows and labels the skill “Four coordinated capabilities”. On `main`, row 5 is `apply-review` (CI → local walkthrough of posted findings), and Flow A/B + Activation already route to it. Dropping that row orphans the sub-skill and breaks agent routing for “what did the CI review say?” / “apply the AI review’s fixes”.

Restore capability #5 and keep Flow/Activation/`Default flow` sibling links consistent with base after rebase.

**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

Version-parity guidance pins `@v1.4.2` and claims identical reviews. Base documents `@v2.1.0` / current major `@v2` and correctly notes that CI may still differ on round 2+ via IAR. Teaching `@v1.4.2` steers new installs onto an obsolete line and overstates local↔CI identity.

After rebase, keep the base pin (`@v2.1.0` or current moving `@v2`) and the IAR caveat.

The Install block still says “Latest v1.x” and pins `npx skills add …@v1.4.2`, and the slug note freezes published tags at `v1.0.0–v1.4.2`. Base already moved this to “Latest v2.x” / `@v2.1.0` and “current major `@v2`”. Copy-paste from this skill would install the wrong major.

Rebase and preserve the v2 Install examples from `main`.

Compressed parity text says “same review, locally and in CI” and removes the entire **CI-only surfaces** block (IAR, `skip-review-label`, incremental follow-up + usage telemetry) that `main` uses to set correct expectations. That is not a lossless compression: agents and humans will treat local full passes as bit-identical to CI round 2+ output.

Keep the Surface-column / audience framing, but retain base’s IAR-aware parity wording and the CI-only surfaces section.

The new “Default flow” header is a good structural idea, but the sibling list says “three sibling sub-skills” and omits `apply-review/SKILL.md`, which base already lists as the fourth sibling. After rebase, keep the header and restore all four siblings (five capabilities total).

summary:
I'd recommend not merging until this branch is rebased onto current `main` — the PR is a stale-branch rewrite that would regress the shipped skill docs, not a pure narrative reframe on top of live content.

## What went wrong

The PR description frames this as a content-only restructure of `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` (522→511 lines, Steps 0–5 “byte-identical”). Against the **actual merge base** (`38c6144`), that is not what the diff does:

| Surface | `main` (base) | This PR (head) |
|---|---|---|
| Frontmatter `version` | `2.5.1` | `1.6.2` |
| Capabilities | **Five** (includes `apply-review`) | **Four** |
| Pin examples | `@v2.1.0` / “Latest v2.x” | `@v1.4.2` / “Latest v1.x” |
| Parity story | methodology + severity; IAR may shorten CI round 2+ | “same review, locally and in CI” |
| CI-only surfaces | IAR, `skip-review-label`, incremental follow-up + usage | **removed** |
| `apply-review/` | present on base (~1.4k LOC sub-skill) | absent from head worktree / router |

The unified diff looks like “Local Companion → Local & CI Companion” only because the branch’s *parent* of the edit was an older four-capability file. Git still merges against today’s `main`, so landing this would overwrite the current router.

## Narrative intent (still good)

The structural goals are sound and already partially present on `main` (two audiences, Surface column, flows-before-install, Default-flow header). After rebase, re-apply **only** any remaining wording polish on top of the five-capability / v2 text — do not resurrect v1.6.2 content.

## Security / skill-audit notes

No new `curl|sh`, token-looking placeholders, or `allowed-tools` expansion in the changed hunks. Trust-boundary Step 0 text is unchanged in intent. Risk is documentation/contract correctness, not a new runtime attack surface.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
